magisterialMasterMasons.name: Master Masons
magisterialMasterMasons.flavor: A guild is a memory of how the last wall was raised.
magisterialMasterMasons.text: Gain +25% production toward Monuments. Completing a culture building for the first time in a city grants 20 production there.

civicGranaries.name: Civic Granaries
civicGranaries.flavor: The stone that marks the square also shades the grain.

theCivicAccounts.name: The Civic Accounts
theCivicAccounts.flavor: What a town writes down, a town can argue about.

magisterialPatronage.name: Patronage
magisterialPatronage.flavor: A court is a promise that talent will be noticed.
magisterialPatronage.text: Your capital gains +1 renown per four citizens. Monuments give +1 culture.

theCivicGuard.name: The Civic Guard
theCivicGuard.flavor: Men who drill under the same stone do not break apart under it.
theCivicGuard.text: Cities with a Monument gain +4 defence. Your military units defending beside one gain +3 strength.
deferred: Towns that keep a Monument are harder to storm.
Soldiers defending beside such a town fight harder. A strength line can be told where the fight is happening — your ground, the hills, a town — but not which buildings stand in the town behind it.

festivalCommissions.name: Festival Commissions
festivalCommissions.flavor: Every new mouth is an excuse for a procession.
festivalCommissions.text: Natural growth in a city with a Monument grants 10 culture and 10 food there.
deferred: a town that holds a monument is paid in song and bread each time it grows
festivalCommissions.note: Not built, on two counts, and both are small. What an occasion hands over is paid to the realm and cannot be told what stands in the town that grew — that is one narrowing on the rider, beside the several it already carries. And the design pays only for growth past a town's own greatest, which is one number on the town. Neither alone frees this row; together they free it and two others.

theTempleOfTheMuses.name: The Temple of the Muses
theTempleOfTheMuses.flavor: Nine sisters, and not one of them keeps accounts.

theSculptorsQuarries.name: The Sculptors' Quarries
theSculptorsQuarries.flavor: The figure was always in the stone; the mason only paid the carter.
theSculptorsQuarries.text: Worked quarries give +1 production and +1 culture. Cities working one gain +15% production toward buildings.

thePageantFields.name: The Pageant Fields
thePageantFields.flavor: The harvest is a rehearsal for the harvest festival.
thePageantFields.text: Worked farms and plantations in cities with a Monument gain +1 food. Cities working at least three such tiles gain +2 culture, once per city.

hearthCeremonies.name: Hearth Ceremonies
hearthCeremonies.flavor: The oldest rite is somebody keeping a fire alight.
hearthCeremonies.text: Cities with a Monument and Shrine gain +2 faith and +2 gold.

magisterialTheWonderFeasts.name: The Wonder-Feasts
magisterialTheWonderFeasts.flavor: Scaffolding draws a crowd, and a crowd must be fed.
magisterialTheWonderFeasts.text: Cities producing a wonder gain +4 food and +2 happiness.

theChronicleOfWorks.name: The Chronicle of Works
theChronicleOfWorks.flavor: A list of what was built is the shortest history there is.
theChronicleOfWorks.text: While active, gains +1 science and +1 gold per turn for each culture building you complete for the first time in a city, at most +30 of each.

theCivicAnnals.name: The Civic Annals
theCivicAnnals.flavor: Year by year, the clerk records that nothing much happened.
theCivicAnnals.text: While active, gains +1 production and +1 culture per turn in your capital each time one of your cities with a Monument grows, at most +24 of each.
deferred: the card keeps count of every time one of your towns that holds a monument grows, and pays a little more each turn for it
theCivicAnnals.note: Not built, on two counts, and the second is the harder. The design pays only for growth past a town's own greatest, which is one number on the town — but a counter is a number on a card and carries no subject at all, so it cannot be told to watch only the towns that hold a monument. Narrowing what a counter counts is a shape nothing else asks for yet.

theCivicNursery.name: The Civic Nursery
theCivicNursery.flavor: A town that raises children can spare a few for the frontier.
theCivicNursery.text: Cities with a Monument produce workers and settlers 20% faster.

publicBenefactors.name: Public Benefactors
publicBenefactors.flavor: The donor's name is carved larger than the building's purpose.
publicBenefactors.text: Purchasing a building with gold in a city with a Monument grants culture equal to 10% of the gold actually paid, at most 30 per purchase. Only its first acquisition in that city qualifies.
deferred: buying a building in a town that holds a monument pays song in proportion to the coin that actually left the treasury, the first time that town acquires one of that kind
publicBenefactors.note: Half built and therefore not built: a purchase now says what it cost and whether it was that town's first, but a windfall is paid to an empire and cannot be told what stands in the town where the money changed hands.

theCourtStewards.name: The Court Stewards
theCourtStewards.flavor: Somebody has to count the spoons.
theCourtStewards.text: Your capital gains +1 food and +1 gold per three citizens while it has a Monument.

theFoundingPageant.name: The Founding Pageant
theFoundingPageant.flavor: First the stone, then the town, then the story about the stone.
theFoundingPageant.text: Founding a city grants a free Monument and 25 culture. Your capital produces settlers 25% faster.

theCapitalOfLetters.name: The Capital of Letters
theCapitalOfLetters.flavor: A city of scribes eats well and marches badly.
theCapitalOfLetters.text: Your capital gains +20% food and +20% gold while it has a Monument and Granary, but trains military units 15% more slowly.

theChancery.name: The Chancery
theChancery.flavor: Every seal is a small argument that somebody has already won.
theChancery.text: Gain +1 authority capacity per two Monuments, at most +3. Cities with at least two culture buildings gain +3 gold.

theCivicStage.name: The Civic Stage
theCivicStage.flavor: The play is old; the audience is not.
theCivicStage.text: Cities with at least two culture buildings gain +2 happiness and +5 food.

thePublicCopyists.name: The Public Copyists
thePublicCopyists.flavor: Twenty hands make twenty books, and twenty-one mistakes.
thePublicCopyists.text: Cities with a Monument and Library gain +5 science and +3 culture.

theArtisanWages.name: The Artisan Wages
theArtisanWages.flavor: Pay the carver and the carving improves.
theArtisanWages.text: Culture buildings give +2 gold and +1 production each.

provincialPatrons.name: Provincial Patrons
provincialPatrons.flavor: The province keeps its own poets, and reads them.
provincialPatrons.text: Noncapital cities with at least two culture buildings gain +1 renown and +3 culture.

theCitizensWatch.name: The Citizens' Watch
theCitizensWatch.flavor: A militia is a town that has decided to stay.
theCitizensWatch.text: Cities with at least two culture buildings train military units 30% faster and gain +3 defence.

theHarbourFestival.name: The Harbour Festival
theHarbourFestival.flavor: Boats dressed in flags catch no fish and sell every seat.
theHarbourFestival.text: Harbours give +3 culture and +3 food. Coastal cities with a Monument gain +1 happiness.

thePageantSchools.name: The Pageant Schools
thePageantSchools.flavor: Children taught the procession will teach it again.
thePageantSchools.text: Cities with a Monument and Temple gain +3 science and +3 faith.

theGrandFairs.name: The Grand Fairs
theGrandFairs.flavor: A fair is a festival that remembered to charge for the stalls.
theGrandFairs.text: Cities with a Market and Monument gain +5 culture and +5 gold.

magisterialTheGroundskeepers.name: The Groundskeepers
magisterialTheGroundskeepers.flavor: The gardener outlasts the genius and keeps the hedges square.
magisterialTheGroundskeepers.text: Worked great-person improvements give +5 food and +5 production.

magisterialTheLaureate.name: The Laureate
magisterialTheLaureate.flavor: A wreath is cheap, and nobody has found anything better.
magisterialTheLaureate.text: Cities working a great-person improvement gain +5 culture, +3 science and +1 renown, once per city.

magisterialTheGuildOfMasons.name: The Guild of Masons
magisterialTheGuildOfMasons.flavor: They will raise anything, and they will be paid on Fridays.
magisterialTheGuildOfMasons.text: Gain +38% production toward wonders. Cities producing a wonder lose 2 gold per turn.

theCivicAssemblies.name: The Civic Assemblies
theCivicAssemblies.flavor: Everyone may speak, and the hall was built for it.
theCivicAssemblies.text: Gain +1 authority capacity per two culture buildings, at most +4. Culture buildings cost 20% less production in noncapital cities.

thePatronsRoad.name: The Patrons' Road
thePatronsRoad.flavor: Money travels to the provinces; taste travels back.
thePatronsRoad.text: Connected noncapital cities with a Monument gain +5 gold and +3 production. Domestic routes from such cities give their destination +3 culture; your foreign routes from them give you +3 culture.

theMasterWorkshops.name: The Master Workshops
theMasterWorkshops.flavor: The workshop is finished last and used first.
theMasterWorkshops.text: Completing a culture building for the first time in a city grants 38 production there and 30 gold.

theCommemorativeFeast.name: The Commemorative Feast
theCommemorativeFeast.flavor: We ate the ox and agreed he had been a great man.
theCommemorativeFeast.text: Spending a great person grants 30 food and 30 production to your nearest city. Each person pays once.
deferred: Spending a great person feeds and supplies the nearest town. The world announces the moment a great person is spent on a deed, and not the moment one is spent laying down a lasting work — so a card written on the spending would pay for half of the ways a person may be spent.

theLivingChronicle.name: The Living Chronicle
theLivingChronicle.flavor: The chronicler is behind, and always will be.
theLivingChronicle.text: While active, gains +2 production and +2 culture per turn in your capital for each wonder you complete or great person you spend, at most +30 of each.
deferred: the card keeps count of the marvels you finish and the great ones you spend, and pays a little more each turn for both
theLivingChronicle.note: Not built: a card may count a marvel finished anywhere in the world and a great one spent, but not a marvel finished by you alone; and two counters cannot share one ceiling, so a card whose limit is on the pair of them cannot be written as a pair of lines.

theCompleteCourt.name: The Complete Court
theCompleteCourt.flavor: A court wants one of everything, and then another.
theCompleteCourt.text: Your capital gains +3% food and +3% production per distinct non-culture building category it holds, at most +18% each.
deferred: Your capital is paid for the breadth of what it has raised. The kinds of building a town holds can be counted now, but not with one of those kinds left out — and this card is paid for everything except its own.

theGreatPatrons.name: The Great Patrons
theGreatPatrons.flavor: The marvel bears his name; the masons bear the stone.
theGreatPatrons.text: Each wonder you hold gives +2 family-neutral renown. Cities containing a wonder purchase culture buildings for 20% less gold.

theMusesCall.name: The Muses' Call
theMusesCall.flavor: They do not come when called; they come when there is somewhere to sit.
theMusesCall.text: Gain +20% renown. Cities working a great-person improvement gain +5 food and +5 production, once per city.

theArtisanCourt.name: The Artisan Court
theArtisanCourt.flavor: The workshop moved into the palace and changed the palace.
theArtisanCourt.text: Cities working a great-person improvement gain +2 renown and purchase culture buildings for 25% less gold.

theWorkingCourt.name: The Working Court
theWorkingCourt.flavor: Applause is pleasant; the scaffolding it pays for is better.
theWorkingCourt.text: Cities with a Monument gain production equal to 30% of their base culture, excluding conversion outputs.

theFestivalSeason.name: The Festival Season
theFestivalSeason.flavor: Four months of holidays, and the accounts to show for it.
theFestivalSeason.text: Cities with a Garden and Amphitheater gain +30% food and +30% gold. Each qualifying city costs +2 gold upkeep.

theCourtArchives.name: The Court Archives
theCourtArchives.flavor: Nothing is thrown away, and nothing is ever found.
theCourtArchives.text: Culture buildings give +3 science each. Cities with at least two gain +8 gold.

thePublicGallery.name: The Public Gallery
thePublicGallery.text: Cities with at least three culture buildings gain +9 food and +3 happiness.

theMonumentalProvinces.name: The Monumental Provinces
theMonumentalProvinces.flavor: The road arrives, and the province discovers it had ambitions.
theMonumentalProvinces.text: Connected noncapital cities with a Monument gain +8 production and +5 culture.

theCivicFaith.name: The Civic Faith
theCivicFaith.flavor: The city is the congregation and the square is the nave.
theCivicFaith.text: Culture buildings give +5 faith each. Cities containing a wonder gain +3 happiness.

theProvincialChancery.name: The Provincial Chancery
theProvincialChancery.flavor: Two clerks in a border town outrank a duke.
theProvincialChancery.text: Gain +1 authority capacity per noncapital city with at least two culture buildings, at most +8. Such cities gain +5 science.

thePalaceGuard.name: The Palace Guard
thePalaceGuard.flavor: Ceremonial armour, sharpened out of habit.
thePalaceGuard.text: Cities with at least three culture buildings train military units 30% faster. Your military units defending those cities gain +4 strength.
deferred: Towns that keep several culture buildings raise soldiers faster and are defended harder. A strength line cannot be told which buildings stand in the town behind it.

theMaritimeGalleries.name: The Maritime Galleries
theMaritimeGalleries.flavor: Every captain's portrait faces the sea he did not drown in.
theMaritimeGalleries.text: Harbours give +8 culture and +5 science. Ships trained in a city with at least two culture buildings gain +3 strength on creation.

theProvincialStages.name: The Provincial Stages
theProvincialStages.flavor: The company tours because the capital is cruel.
theProvincialStages.text: Noncapital cities with at least two culture buildings gain +2 renown and +5 food.

magisterialTheMastersPresence.name: The Master's Presence
magisterialTheMastersPresence.flavor: He is difficult, and the work is better while he is difficult here.
magisterialTheMastersPresence.text: Cities working a great-person improvement gain +30% production toward buildings and +23% gold.

theGrandTour.name: The Grand Tour
theGrandTour.flavor: Young men are sent abroad to come home with opinions.
theGrandTour.text: Cities containing a wonder gain +8 culture and +8 science. Cities working a great-person improvement gain +2 happiness.

theLearnedPatron.name: The Learned Patron
theLearnedPatron.flavor: He funds the study and reads only the dedication.
theLearnedPatron.text: Cities with at least two culture buildings gain science equal to 15% of their base culture, at most +18 science per city. Conversion outputs are excluded.

thePerformersTreasury.name: The Performers' Treasury
thePerformersTreasury.flavor: The troupe keeps a strongbox and a grudge.
thePerformersTreasury.text: Cities with at least two culture buildings gain gold equal to 30% of their base culture, excluding conversion outputs.

theCivicHarvest.name: The Civic Harvest
theCivicHarvest.flavor: A great town eats like a province and says grace like a village.
theCivicHarvest.text: Cities of at least ten population with at least two culture buildings gain +38% food and +3 happiness, and retain an additional 20% of food spent on growth.

theSenateCharter.name: The Senate Charter
theSenateCharter.flavor: They meet where the government sits, and nowhere else will do.
theSenateCharter.text: Unlocks the capital-only Assembly Hall. A city with one gains +3 happiness and +30% production toward buildings.

theSculptorsSchools.name: The Sculptors' Schools
theSculptorsSchools.flavor: The pupil copies the master until the copy is wanted instead.
theSculptorsSchools.text: Worked great-person improvements give +5 science and +5 gold. Their cities gain +1 renown, once per city.

thePatronsFleet.name: The Patrons' Fleet
thePatronsFleet.flavor: A hull with a poet aboard sails no faster and is remembered longer.
thePatronsFleet.text: Cities with a Harbour and at least two culture buildings train ships 53% faster. Your ships gain +1 movement.

theCulturalEmbassies.name: The Cultural Embassies
theCulturalEmbassies.flavor: An ambassador is a spy who has been introduced.
theCulturalEmbassies.text: Each foreign empire you have met and are at peace with gives your capital +3 gold and +2 culture, at most +12 gold and +8 culture. Gain +1 family-neutral renown per two such partners, at most +2.
deferred: Your capital is paid for each foreign realm you have met and are not fighting. Nothing counts the realms you have met, nor the ones you are at peace with — only the ones your caravans trade with.

theMonumentalCourt.name: The Monumental Court
theMonumentalCourt.flavor: One marvel makes a town; two make a capital of something.
theMonumentalCourt.text: Cities containing a wonder gain +3 renown and +38% production toward culture buildings and wonders, once per city.

theCivicCommonwealth.name: The Civic Commonwealth
theCivicCommonwealth.flavor: A town that governs itself is cheaper to govern.
theCivicCommonwealth.text: Cities with at least three culture buildings demand 20% less population happiness and cost one less authority, minimum one.

theGreatExhibition.name: The Great Exhibition
theGreatExhibition.flavor: Everything the realm can make, under one roof, for a season.
theGreatExhibition.text: Worked great-person improvements gain +25% of their native yield. Cities working at least two different types gain +20% gold.
deferred: Great-person works pay half again as much as they were built to pay.
Towns working several different kinds of such work earn more. The kinds a town works can be counted and paid for one at a time, but a town cannot yet be admitted for working several of them.

theGoldenAge.name: The Golden Age
theGoldenAge.flavor: Afterwards everyone agreed it had been one.
theGoldenAge.text: Completing a wonder gives your cities +20% production and culture for ten turns. A later wonder restarts the ten turns.
theGoldenAge.note: A wonder completed while the bonus runs starts it again, and does not add a second bonus. The Magnum Opus is not a wonder.

theLaureateCities.name: The Laureate Cities
theLaureateCities.flavor: Big enough to argue about itself in public.
theLaureateCities.text: Cities of at least twelve population with at least two culture buildings gain +38% culture and +15% science.

theNationalGalleries.name: The National Galleries
theNationalGalleries.flavor: The realm buys back what its own towns sold abroad.
theNationalGalleries.text: Culture buildings give +5 food and +5 gold each. Cities with at least three gain +4 happiness.

theProvincialAcademies.name: The Provincial Academies
theProvincialAcademies.flavor: The best lecture halls are three weeks from the court.
theProvincialAcademies.text: Connected noncapital cities with a Library and at least two culture buildings gain +30% production and +15% science.

theCivicPantheon.name: The Civic Pantheon
theCivicPantheon.flavor: Room enough under one dome for everybody's god.
theCivicPantheon.text: Cities containing a wonder gain +25% faith and +20% gold. Wonders give +10 culture each.

magisterialTheSalon.name: The Salon
magisterialTheSalon.flavor: Six chairs, one argument, and a century of consequences.
magisterialTheSalon.text: Culture buildings give +2 renown each in cities working a great-person improvement, at most +6 per city.
deferred: Culture buildings pay renown in towns whose citizens work a great person's lasting work. A trickle counted off a shelf of buildings is counted across the whole realm, and cannot be held to a class of town or to a ceiling in each one.

magisterialTheMagistersCourt.name: The Magister's Court
magisterialTheMagistersCourt.flavor: The last work is begun where the first one still stands.
magisterialTheMagistersCourt.text: Cities containing a wonder gain +25% production toward the Magnum Opus.
magisterialTheMagistersCourt.note: A town you captured that holds a wonder counts too.

theMastersDomain.name: The Masters' Domain
theMastersDomain.flavor: The estate outlived the man and kept his standards.
theMastersDomain.text: Worked great-person works give +3 food and +3 production.

theGreatChancery.name: The Great Chancery
theGreatChancery.flavor: An empire is whatever its clerks can keep track of.
theGreatChancery.text: Gain +2 authority capacity per city with at least three culture buildings, at most +12. Such cities gain +30% culture.

theImperialPageant.name: The Imperial Pageant
theImperialPageant.flavor: The parade goes past the monuments on purpose.
theImperialPageant.text: Your military units gain +5 strength when defending within two hexes of your wonder or great-person work. Cities with at least three culture buildings train military units 35% faster.
deferred: Soldiers defending near your marvels and your great people's works fight harder. A strength line can be told whose ground the fight is on, but not what stands two hexes away from it.
Towns that keep several culture buildings raise soldiers faster.

theHonouredDead.name: The Honoured Dead
theHonouredDead.flavor: The tombs are in the capital because the capital insisted.
theHonouredDead.text: While seated, this card gains +2 science and +4 production in your capital each time you spend a great person, up to +30 science and +60 production.

thePageantsOfPeace.name: The Pageants of Peace
thePageantsOfPeace.flavor: A quiet border is the most expensive thing a realm can own.
thePageantsOfPeace.text: While at peace with every foreign empire, cities with at least two culture buildings gain +30% culture and +2 happiness.

theLivingCanon.name: The Living Canon
theLivingCanon.flavor: The list of masters is revised by people who are not on it.
theLivingCanon.text: Your cities gain +4% food and +4% production per distinct great-person family whose legacy you currently hold, at most +20% each.

theUniversalCourt.name: The Universal Court
theUniversalCourt.flavor: Everything the realm believes, arranged for visitors.
theUniversalCourt.text: Cities with at least three culture buildings gain food and gold each equal to 38% of their base culture. Conversion outputs are excluded.

theLastCommission.name: The Last Commission
theLastCommission.flavor: One more, the patron said, and meant it this time.
theLastCommission.text: Spending a great person grants the city building your Magnum Opus 150 production, at most once per turn. No Opus under construction means no payout. Each person can pay once.
deferred: spending a great person sends production to the town building your Magnum Opus, at most once a turn
theLastCommission.note: Waiting on a new moment. The game does not yet mark the moment a great person is spent, and it cannot yet hold back the production when no town is building the Magnum Opus.

theWonderCommonwealth.name: The Wonder Commonwealth
theWonderCommonwealth.flavor: Some towns keep the marvels; the rest keep the memory.
theWonderCommonwealth.text: Cities containing a wonder gain +38% production and +38% food. Your cities without a wonder gain +15% culture instead.

thePrytaneion.name: The Prytaneion
thePrytaneion.flavor: Whoever served the city ate at its table, and the city paid.
thePrytaneion.text: Each town gains +1 food for each card you have seated.
thePrytaneion.note: Only the Orders sitting in a chair count, this one included. A charter takes no chair, so it does not count, and neither does a Doctrine.

thePolemarch.name: The Polemarch
thePolemarch.flavor: One of the nine magistrates led the army, and the other eight gave advice.
thePolemarch.text: Your units gain +2 strength for each Military card you have seated.
thePolemarch.note: Every unit gains it, on land and at sea, attacking or defending. This card counts itself, and a Military card in a Wildcard chair counts too.

theCourtPainter.name: The Court Painter
theCourtPainter.flavor: Every new minister sits for a portrait, so the painter is never short of work.
theCourtPainter.text: Each card you draft grants 15 renown. A charter counts.
theCourtPainter.note: A card picked from a free hand counts. Passing on a hand does not, and neither does a Doctrine or a great person. This card pays nothing for drafting itself.

theCornerstone.name: The Cornerstone
theCornerstone.flavor: The first stone is laid with a speech, and the rest are laid in silence.
theCornerstone.text: Towns that hold no wonder build wonders 30% faster.

theRepertory.name: The Repertory
theRepertory.flavor: The same plays every season, and the same people cry at the same lines.

theSecondReading.name: The Second Reading
theSecondReading.flavor: A law read twice is a law somebody has thought about.
theSecondReading.text: The first reroll of each hand is free.
theSecondReading.note: This covers hands of Orders, Doctrines and great people, and it lets you reroll before you know Chronology. A belief hand's first reroll is already free.

theNomarchs.name: The Nomarchs
theNomarchs.flavor: Each province had its governor, and each governor had a seat at court.
theNomarchs.text: +1 authority for every two cards you have seated.
theNomarchs.note: Only the Orders sitting in a chair count, this one included. A charter takes no chair, so it does not count, and neither does a Doctrine.

theWorkshopAtOlympia.name: The Workshop at Olympia
theWorkshopAtOlympia.flavor: The sculptor's shed still stands beside the temple, long after the statue went.
theWorkshopAtOlympia.text: +2 renown a turn for each wonder you hold.

theOverseersOfWorks.name: The Overseers of Works
theOverseersOfWorks.flavor: When a master arrives, the stone yards are already waiting.
theOverseersOfWorks.text: Each time you gain a great person, your capital gains 100 production for each age you have reached.

theSitingMasters.name: The Siting Masters
theSitingMasters.flavor: They walk the ground for a week before a single stake goes in.
theSitingMasters.text: Great-person works gain +1 culture for each hill, mountain, forest or water hex beside them, at most +3.
theSitingMasters.note: A hex counts once, even when it is two of these, such as a forested hill.

theKeepersOfWonders.name: The Keepers of Wonders
theKeepersOfWonders.flavor: People sleep better near a thing that will outlast them.
theKeepersOfWonders.text: +2 happiness for each wonder you hold.

theCeremonialGuard.name: The Ceremonial Guard
theCeremonialGuard.flavor: The armour is polished for the visitors, and the spears are sharp for everyone else.
theCeremonialGuard.text: Towns holding a wonder gain +5 defence.

theUnveiling.name: The Unveiling
theUnveiling.flavor: The cloth comes down, the crowd draws breath, and the council sits again.
theUnveiling.text: Completing a wonder deals you a free Order hand.
theUnveiling.note: No hand is dealt while an Order hand or a Doctrine offer is waiting for your answer. The free hand does not raise the price of your next hand.

theEncyclopedia.name: The Encyclopedia
theEncyclopedia.flavor: Everything known, in order from A to Z, and still not finished.
theEncyclopedia.text: +1 science and +1 culture in your capital for each Order you hold unseated, at most +15 of each.
theEncyclopedia.note: A charter counts, because it never takes a chair.

thePrefects.name: The Prefects
thePrefects.flavor: One kept the grain coming, one kept the fires out, and one kept the provinces paying.
thePrefects.text: +5% production for each Economic card you have seated.
thePrefects.note: This card counts itself, and an Economic card in a Wildcard chair counts too.

theSymposium.name: The Symposium
theSymposium.flavor: The wine went round, and so did the ideas, and somebody always wrote them down.
theSymposium.text: Each time you gain a great person, you are dealt a free Order hand.
theSymposium.note: No hand is dealt while an Order hand or a Doctrine offer is waiting for your answer. The free hand does not raise the price of your next hand.

lettersPatent.name: Letters Patent
lettersPatent.flavor: An open letter under the great seal, which anyone may read and nobody may refuse.
lettersPatent.text: Your great people's acts pay 50% more.
lettersPatent.note: It raises the gold, production, science and culture an act pays. A general's act pays none of these, so it gains nothing.

magisterialTheQuarterOfMasters.name: The Quarter of Masters
magisterialTheQuarterOfMasters.flavor: Put two masters on one street and watch.
magisterialTheQuarterOfMasters.text: A great-person work beside another great-person work yields its own yield again. This never stacks.
magisterialTheQuarterOfMasters.note: The work's own yield is paid again once, however many works stand beside it. What other cards pay on the work is not paid again.

theGazetteers.name: The Gazetteers
theGazetteers.flavor: They list every marvel in the province, and the tax collectors read the list.
theGazetteers.text: +3% production and gold for each great-person work in your borders, at most +30%.
theGazetteers.note: A work counts whether or not a town works its hex. A prophet's holy site is a great-person work too.

theSevenSights.name: The Seven Sights
theSevenSights.flavor: Travellers came a long way to see seven things, and paid for their supper at every one.
theSevenSights.text: +5% culture and science for each wonder you hold, at most +30%.

theBoule.name: The Boule
theBoule.flavor: Five hundred citizens, chosen by lot, met on every day the city needed them.
theBoule.text: +2% science and culture for each card you have seated.
theBoule.note: Only the Orders sitting in a chair count, this one included. A charter takes no chair, so it does not count, and neither does a Doctrine.

theRollOfMasters.name: The Roll of Masters
theRollOfMasters.flavor: Each name on the roll makes the next one easier to find.
theRollOfMasters.text: +3% science and culture for each great person you have gained this game, at most +30%.
theRollOfMasters.note: A great person counts from the moment you gain it, spent or not. Great people gained before this card was seated count too.

theGardenCourts.name: The Garden Courts
theGardenCourts.flavor: Between the studios, a garden, and in the garden, an argument.
theGardenCourts.text: Towns working at least two great-person works gain +20% culture and science.

thePrivyCouncil.name: The Privy Council
thePrivyCouncil.flavor: The council met in private, so nobody saw how much it decided.
thePrivyCouncil.text: Each of your cards that pays production pays +1 more production wherever it pays it.
thePrivyCouncil.note: Each town, hex or empire line counts on its own, so a card that pays production in many towns gains in each of them. A percentage is not raised, and this card does not raise itself.

theBulwarkOfMarvels.name: The Bulwark of Marvels
theBulwarkOfMarvels.flavor: The walls are thickest where the city keeps what it cannot build twice.
theBulwarkOfMarvels.text: The town building your Magnum Opus gains +4 defence for each wonder you hold.
theBulwarkOfMarvels.note: Every wonder you hold counts, in any of your towns, and a wonder you captured counts too.
